what_this_is: The invariant contract of a clean-room database that may carry business data.
expected_counts.json describes the database immediately after `build`: exact counts, one
operator, zero opportunities. Those are the right assertions for a fresh rebuild and only
then. origenlab_clean has carried operator decisions since 2026-09-24 — evidence reviews, the
historical quotation import, the campaign import — and every one of them moves a count that
file declares. That is not drift to be re-baselined: a count that changes whenever a human
decides something is not a contract, and a fixture rewritten to today's numbers would be
stale by the next decision and would prove nothing about the next rebuild.
Every probe below is emitted by supabase/cleanroom/data_bearing.sql and compared by
supabase/cleanroom/compare.py, exact in both directions. Each one is decided by the
migration chain, the role bootstrap or a grant — never by how many rows a table holds. The
chain probes compare the ledger against the files in supabase/migrations/ as the caller
passes them, so a migration added on disk and not applied fails here without this file
changing. The inventory numbers (50 tables, 173 policies, the closed SECURITY DEFINER
list) are the same constants verify_chain.sh, docs/DOMAIN.md §7 and docs/STATUS.md §2.1
carry; a migration that moves one moves all of them in the same PR.
Historical business data is allowed. No probe here counts a business row.

migrations.missing_from_ledger.why: every file in supabase/migrations/ has its ledger row. A version listed here is a migration that exists on disk and was never applied to this database — the state a data-bearing database is in the moment canonical main gains a migration, and the reason verify must run after every apply.

migrations.not_in_supabase_migrations.why: no ledger row names a version that is not on disk. A version here means the database was migrated from a branch that never merged, or a file was renamed after it was applied (the campaign-block migration was renamed before it reached origenlab_clean, precisely so this would stay empty).

migrations.ledger_has_duplicates.why: version is the ledger's primary key; a duplicate can only mean the ledger table itself was replaced.

schemas.present.why: the seven private schemas (docs/DOMAIN.md §7), all present, none extra among them.

tables.count.why: the inventory at head 20261005140628 (docs/DOMAIN.md §7, docs/STATUS.md §2.1). Same constant as verify_chain.sh.

tables.by_schema.why: the total alone would not notice a table moved between schemas.

tables.without_rls.why: row-level security is enabled on every table; a table created outside the chain, or one whose RLS was disabled to make a load easier, shows here.

tables.not_owned_by_origenlab_owner.why: every table is owned by the NOLOGIN owner role; a table owned by postgres or by a login role escapes the grant matrix.

policies.count.why: the policy inventory at head 20261005140628: the 160 of 20260930120000 (docs/STATUS.md §2.7.39), the six origenlab_api policies on catalog.product_image and catalog.supplier_terms (20261005134832), and the seven origenlab_api policies on catalog.fx_rate, catalog.cost_parameter and evidence.document_line (20261005140628). Same constant as verify_chain.sh.

policies.platform.why: the platform policies by name and command. Note what is absent: no runtime INSERT or UPDATE policy on platform.operator (20260928192000), no UPDATE policy on auth_principal or operator_profile (20260928194000) — the throttle is written only through the definers.

foreign_keys.without_covering_index.why: every foreign key's referencing columns lead some index (090_foreign_key_indexes.sql proves the same on a fresh chain).

roles.origenlab.why: the four roles of supabase/roles.sql, no fifth.

roles.with_forbidden_attribute.why: MIGRATION.md §5.2 check 1: no OrigenLab role bypasses RLS or holds SUPERUSER, CREATEROLE, CREATEDB or REPLICATION.

roles.owner_can_login.why: origenlab_owner is NOLOGIN; it is reached only by SET ROLE inside a migration.

roles.owner_holds_database_create.why: M14 revoked CREATE on the database from the owner; a schema can only come from the chain.

grants.schema_usage_held_by_public_roles.why: MIGRATION.md §5.2 check 3: PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role hold USAGE on none of the seven schemas.

grants.table_privilege_held_by_public_ro.why: check 4, at table and column level: those four roles hold no privilege on any table.

grants.function_execute_held_by_public_r.why: those four roles can EXECUTE nothing in the seven schemas — PostgreSQL grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default, so every function must have revoked it.

grants.default_privileges_for_public_rol.why: check 5: no ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES hands those roles anything created later.

functions.security_definer.why: the closed list (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2), by signature. A fourth definer is a new privileged path and must be reviewed as one; a missing one means a migration was not applied.

functions.security_definer_misconfigured.why: each definer is owned by origenlab_owner, pins search_path to pg_catalog, is executable by origenlab_api and by neither origenlab_worker nor origenlab_migrator. Any deviation counts once per function.

functions.not_owned_by_origenlab_owner.why: a function owned by another role is outside the chain's ownership model.

functions.record_pin_attempt_present.why: 20260929100000 dropped platform.record_pin_attempt: called directly as origenlab_api it cleared both failure counters with no PIN (docs/STATUS.md §2.7.38). Its presence means that migration did not run.

auth.tables_present.why: the four sign-in tables of slice 1 (#38–#41) exist. They may be empty — they are, until a principal and profiles are provisioned — but the contract is that they exist with the boundary below.

auth.api_execute_begin_pin_attempt.why: the runtime role begins a PIN attempt only through the definer.

auth.api_execute_finish_pin_attempt.why: and finishes it only through the definer; without this EXECUTE no operator could ever sign in.

auth.api_execute_hmac_sha256.why: the HMAC helper is INVOKER and executable by its owner alone; the runtime role must not be able to compute a proof outside finish_pin_attempt.

auth.api_select_pin_hash.why: the stored verifier is never readable by the runtime role. Before 20260929100000 it was, through a table-level SELECT that a column REVOKE could not override.

auth.api_select_operator_profile_table_l.why: the table-level SELECT is gone; only named columns are granted. A table-level grant would silently re-cover pin_hash.

auth.api_operator_profile_columns_not_re.why: every column but pin_hash is granted by name; a column added by a later migration and not granted would break the profile roster, so it is counted here.

auth.api_updates_auth_principal.why: no UPDATE, table- or column-level: the throttle counters on the principal are written only inside the definers (20260928194000, re-asserted by 20260929100000).

auth.api_updates_operator_profile.why: the same for the profile row.

auth.api_writes_operator.why: 20260928192000: the runtime role neither inserts nor updates platform.operator; operators are provisioned by profile_roster.py as the migrator.

auth.api_deletes_in_platform.why: nothing in platform.* is deletable by the runtime role; audit and receipts are append-only.

auth.api_auth_session_updatable_columns.why: a session can be revoked and nothing else about it changed (20260928191000).

auth.api_auth_session_insert_select.why: the runtime role opens and reads sessions.

auth.api_auth_event_insert_select_only.why: the audit trail is append-only for the runtime role: INSERT and SELECT, no UPDATE on any column.

auth.worker_reaches_sign_in_tables.why: origenlab_worker has no privilege on any of the four sign-in tables; sign-in is the API's alone.

outbound.send_control.any_flag_enabled.why: a local database must never be able to send, whatever else it holds.

residue.source_record_pytest.why: dedupe_key like 'pytest-%' — the fixture residue that quarantined origenlab_dev on 2026-09-22 is caught by name in any database, data-bearing or not.

residue.operator_pytest.why: email_norm like 'pytest-%', for the same reason.
